youtube.title: black-ice — dark 90s club techno for a 1995 hacker movie, 132 BPM
youtube.description:
Mid-90s club techno: dark, hypnotic and mechanical, 132 BPM in A minor, written for the soundtrack of a 1995 cyberpunk hacker movie that never existed. A 909 groove, a rolling analog bass, a resonant five-note sequence, and the air and voices of Nine Inch Nails recordings.

Six ideas, and nothing new after the first minute. The kick, the bass ostinato, the motif, a high glass sequence, the air and the voice are arranged rather than added to: filters open and close over whole sections, parts drop out and return, the drums thin and come back. The motif never follows the one chord change (A minor to F to G), so it stays a machine while the bass moves under it. The air is sampled: held strings and a drone from Demon Seed, a dub echo and three wordless screams from Ghosts 38, each fading in under the parts rather than over them.

Written as text, mixed by measurement, rendered in the browser.

Chapters
0:00 Kick and hat
0:15 The bass arrives
0:29 The groove whole
0:44 The first voice
0:58 Break — no kick
1:13 Payoff
1:56 Variation
2:11 Second break
2:40 Peak — everything at once
3:24 Out

Play and edit this song in your browser at jonborchardt.github.io/strudel-bench — press play, drag a slider, change a note, hear it immediately. Nothing to install.

Every song here is a text file. This one is songs/black-ice.strudel in the repo, along with the harness that plays it:
https://github.com/jonborchardt/strudel-bench

strudel-bench is a live-coding harness where a song is a text file written in a high-level language: parts, sections, and twelve musical axes (density, brightness, weight, space, articulation and so on) that a phrase like "darker and more spacious" can move. Most of the code and the songs were written by coding agents working from a written spec, in the spirit of my blog, "always shippable, always improving":
https://jonborchardt.github.io/blog/

The video is not a screen recording. It is generated from the song itself: every hit in the music drives the animation, and the world it plays in is chosen from the song's own musical features.

Built on Strudel, the JavaScript port of TidalCycles: https://strudel.cc
Samples come from the public Strudel packs, each under its own license: https://strudel.cc/learn/samples/
The strings, drone, echo and voices are sampled from Nine Inch Nails' multitracks of Demon Seed (The Slip) and 38 Ghosts (Ghosts I-IV), released under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, and this track is shared under the same license:
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/3.0/

prompt: radio-quality mid-90s techno / progressive house, 132 bpm A minor, ~5:49, six objects arranged by filter, mute and density; NIN atmosphere and wordless vocals from the sound store as colour, never the lead

requests.ask: more ambient NIN sounds, vocals sparingly and always accompanied, not the main attraction; a 1994-96 club techno track from six core objects

changes.why: packs black-ice-cuts: Demon Seed strings (A3) and E drone, Ghosts 38 dub echo, three wordless Ghosts 38 vocal takes; loops written as bars 3 and 6 since both source songs are 6/4 at 132
melody motif '0 ~ ~ 7 ~ ~ 4 ~ ~ 2 ~ ~ 7 ~ 4 ~' five notes on a dotted-eighth grid, never following the chords; the filter ramps and wobbles over 16-bar sections
bass notes two-bar rolling ostinato resting on every kick, root and fifth with an octave pop, ducked under the kick

mix kit .55>.4, bass .6>.75, motif .5>.85, glass .35>.9/1, drone 1.4>1, echo .55>.4, strings .6>.4, pad .4>.35: measure had the kit 1.6 dB under the mix, the motif 16 down, the glass 27.6 down, the air masking itself; now kit -2.9, bass -7.2, motif -10, glass -18, air -15..-18

voice ah level 1.1>.55, swell 1>.6, tick .35>.15: the held ah measured 4.4 dB under the mix, the loudest thing in the break; now the motif and strings carry it at -5.5 and the voice sits at -7.9 under them

requests.ask: make the first 5 sections half as long

changes.why: cycles 16>8: the build to the payoff halved, 1:13 instead of 2:25; the song is now 152 bars, about 4:36
voice: breath moved to the end of bar 4, the ah to bar 5 (were bars 8 and 9 of 16)
voice: breath to bar 4, the reversed ah swell to bar 5 so it still ends into the payoff (were bars 8 and 13 of 16)
cycles 8>2: the reduction takes 8 bars instead of 32; the song is now 128 bars, about 3:53
sweep 4>2: the closing filter sweep spans the whole two-bar section

requests.ask: raw and raw2 (the screams) need to be way less abrupt, maybe longer, start quiet

changes.why: voice: the three Ghosts 38 takes are screams, not breaths; every one now fades in instead of starting hard
raw cry: attack .7 s, speed .5 (about 1.4 s, an octave down), lpf 3 kHz, echo feedback .45>.55, moved to beat 3 so it rises into the next bar; level 1.1>.8
raw2 held cry: attack 1.5 s, clip 3 and release 2.5 s so it swells in and fades out over its whole length instead of cutting
raw2 chop: slices attack .08 release .3, lpf 2.5 kHz, level .9>.6
raw removed: the short cry is gone from the first vocal section; the held cry on bar five is its only voice
raw3 removed: no reversed swell into the payoff; the riser alone leads into it

requests.ask: variation raw2 needs to be quieter or wobble or something

changes.why: raw2 chop level .6>.35, lpf sine 700..2200 Hz over two bars, pan sine .15..85 over two bars: quieter and moving instead of stabbing in one place

requests.ask: peak raw needs quieter or something

changes.why: raw cry level .8>.45, twice instead of three times (bars 8 and 24), lpf sine 800..2400 Hz over four bars: under the parts instead of over them

requests.ask: drums mess up 2 s in; bass quietly at the end of the intro; break remove raw; variation raw2 throughout

changes.why: perc2 rim rhythm .xxx>.x.x (e and a only), timing drift 6>3 ms: its middle sixteenth sat on the hat's offbeat and flammed against it as the rim faded in, about bar two (the trace showed no dropouts, 9% busy)
bass added: level .45, brightness ramp 0>.22, so the line is heard only toward the end of the intro
raw removed: no short cry in the first break
raw2 chop through all sixteen bars instead of bars seven and eight
raw2 chop every other bar instead of every bar: 2.5 hits a bar on average instead of 5
cycles 16>8, its cry moved from bar 16 to bar 8 so it still closes the section; the song is now 120 bars, about 3:38

requests.ask: out 1 2 3 4 is too much, just have 2 of them, make it sound right

changes.why: (2 bars each) > out1, out2 (4 bars each): out1 keeps the groove, bass and motif with the motif's filter closing .55>.08, the open hat and drone gone; out2 is kick, hats and rim with the bass closing .3>0 and a two-bar sweep to the end; still 8 bars, 120 in all

requests.ask: do a final mix; visuals loom with an occasional overlay (rave, not signal); keep the pack to what the song uses

changes.why: raw noise gain .035>.45: measured 46.7 dB under the mix, now 23.7
perc2 rim level .4>.25: it sat above the hats
raw2 level .55>.35: the held cry measured level with the motif and strings (-6 dB), now -9.3 under them
drums level .45>.25: the filtered kick was the loudest part of the break (-1.7), now -4 and the strings, pad and motif carry it
visual overlay loom + rave: loom full frame, rave breathing in every eight bars, strongest in the loud sections
mix whole render: rms .126 (-18 dBFS), peak .972 on kick transients, no clipped samples; every section's mix lint clean

requests.ask: make the overlay less often; commit when done

changes.why: visual every 32 (new visual.every in lib/song.mjs, lib/visual.mjs and web/visual/director.mjs): rave visits over loom for eight bars once every thirty-two (intro, first break, variation, the start of the peak) instead of every eight
room size 1.1>.9: the room impulse is 0.9 s, so a longer size asked for a tail it does not have (test/check caught it)
